candidates.decision_relevance: A complete settled ETF-flow and breadth sequence would materially test whether proxy breadth and price weakness were confirmed or contradicted by the intended completed-week evidence.
candidates.evidence_reference: W33-W37 weekly adversarial reviews; daily outputs repeatedly identify settled ETF data as unavailable or stale.
candidates.missing_history_problem: Only isolated, stale settled sessions are available; within-week sequencing, persistence, concentration, and the relationship between ETF flows and price participation cannot be audited.

candidates.decision_relevance: A stable-universe broad breadth history would distinguish broad participation from narrow ETH or selected-asset strength and test whether proxy breadth deterioration preceded price weakness.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily outputs repeatedly state that top-100 breadth is point-in-time, membership-changing, proxy-only, and non-canonical; weekly reviews cite missing broad participation and leadership data.
candidates.missing_history_problem: Existing breadth observations are endpoint snapshots with changing membership, preventing persistence, lead-lag, and broad-versus-narrow participation assessment.

candidates.decision_relevance: Point-in-time intraday price, breadth, flow, depth, funding, open-interest, and liquidation histories would establish whether deterioration led or followed drawdowns and whether rebounds were durable.
candidates.evidence_reference: W33-W37 reviews and daily outputs repeatedly identify missing timestamp-aligned sequences, unavailable 1-hour anchors, shortened nominal windows, and fragile liquidation observations.
candidates.missing_history_problem: The supplied record contains snapshots and overlapping horizon returns but not a continuous, cutoff-aligned sequence; sequence error, hindsight contamination, and cross-horizon disagreement therefore remain unresolved.

candidates.decision_relevance: The frozen forecast-candidate archive would permit direct audit of ex-ante availability, target precision, horizon alignment, overlap, and broad-range containment.
candidates.evidence_reference: All weekly reviews report three prior candidates but receive empty forecast_candidates arrays; daily outputs contain current unratified candidates only.
candidates.missing_history_problem: Issue times, evidence cutoffs, metric paths, bounds, targets, thresholds, rationales, and confidence fields for prior candidates are absent, preventing falsifiability and hindsight-leakage audits.

candidates.decision_relevance: Matured candidate outcomes and warning records would provide the missing empirical evidence for false positives, false negatives, opportunity cost, and calibration of the descriptive warnings.
candidates.evidence_reference: W33-W37 reviews and daily outputs report null or zero matured outcomes and zero matured exit/action-compass rows.
candidates.missing_history_problem: No candidate-specific realized outcomes or matured warning episodes are available, so prior cautionary language cannot be empirically evaluated and missingness cannot be treated as clean performance.

candidates.decision_relevance: Historical cross-sectional leadership and liquidity participation would distinguish broad alt-led expansion from narrow ETH/BTC relative strength or distribution.
candidates.evidence_reference: Weekly reviews explicitly state that ETH/BTC strength alone cannot distinguish PARABOLIC_ALTSEASON from DISTRIBUTION because broad participation, leadership persistence, spot-volume confirmation, and liquidity dispersion are missing.
candidates.missing_history_problem: Current rotation scores and ETH/BTC observations lack asset-level participation, leadership breadth, spot-volume confirmation, and liquidity dispersion history needed to identify whether relative strength broadened.

candidates.decision_relevance: Complete venue-covered liquidation and positioning histories would clarify whether deleveraging was predominantly long or short, whether it preceded recovery, and whether reported stress was merely a lower-bound artifact.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily and weekly documents repeatedly describe liquidation aggregates as lower bounds from fragile legacy REST windows with unverified completeness; open-interest changes are also directionally ambiguous.
candidates.missing_history_problem: Existing liquidation data may be truncated and do not provide reliable composition or persistence, while open-interest snapshots cannot distinguish deleveraging, short covering, contract effects, or renewed leverage.
